summary: Implemented the SSH adapter: a RemoteExecutor trait backed by OpenSshExecutor (controlled process execution of Windows OpenSSH, BatchMode=yes, ConnectTimeout, args passed separately never string-interpolated), a hard-timeout-enforcing process primitive verified against real OS processes, an SshError classification enum mapping onto DeviceConnectionStatus, the RemoteOperation catalogue (Probe wired up now; SystemIdentity/SystemMetrics/DockerContainers reserved for M3), and a FakeRemoteExecutor test double covering all five required simulation scenarios. 30 new Rust unit tests, 64 total passing; also manually cross-checked the classification heuristics against this machine's real ssh.exe output.
completed: domain/connection_status.rs: DeviceConnectionStatus enum matching spec section 9.3.
infrastructure/ssh/process.rs: run_with_timeout() -- SSH-agnostic hard-timeout enforcement via try_wait() polling + kill on deadline, unit-tested against real cmd/ping processes (not just mocked).
infrastructure/ssh/operation.rs: RemoteOperation catalogue (Probe, SystemIdentity, SystemMetrics, DockerContainers); only Probe has a command body now.

infrastructure/ssh/error.rs: SshError (DnsResolutionError/ConnectionRefused/ConnectionTimeout/AuthenticationError/HostKeyError/RemoteCommandError/RemoteCommandTimeout/Spawn) + to_connection_status() mapping; HostKeyError always maps to HostKeyError, never auto-resolved.

infrastructure/ssh/openssh.rs: OpenSshExecutor building `ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=<n> -p <port> <user>@<host> <command>` with every arg passed separately; classify_outcome() interprets exit code 255 + stderr text into the right SshError.
infrastructure/ssh/executor.rs: RemoteExecutor trait, RemoteExecutionResult/SshTarget types, default probe() method.
infrastructure/ssh/fake.rs (test-only): FakeRemoteExecutor with online/offline/timeout/authentication_error/host_key_error constructors for this and future (M3) tests.
Module marked #[allow(dead_code, unused_imports)] since nothing calls into it yet -- WU008 wires up the connection-test command.

Manually ran real ssh.exe against a nonexistent host and a closed port on this machine to confirm the DNS-resolution and connection-refused stderr patterns match classify_outcome's assumptions before committing.
Verified cargo test (64/64, 30 new), cargo build (no warnings), and npm run build all pass.

validationCommands.summary: Unaffected by this backend-only work unit; still succeeds.

validationCommands.command: manual: ssh.exe against a nonexistent host and a closed local port
validationCommands.summary: Confirmed exit code 255 with stderr text matching classify_outcome's DNS-resolution and connection-refused detection exactly.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: A fake RemoteExecutor can be substituted in tests to simulate online, offline, timeout, authentication failure, and host-key failure
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: FakeRemoteExecutor::online/offline/timeout/authentication_error/host_key_error, each with a passing test asserting probe() returns the expected Ok/Err.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Host-key errors are never auto-resolved or bypassed
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: host_key_error_never_maps_to_a_resolved_status test; classify_outcome only ever produces SshError::HostKeyError for host-key stderr patterns, and there is no code path anywhere in this module that clears, retries past, or silently accepts a host-key failure.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Every remote execution enforces a hard timeout
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: enforces_a_hard_timeout_and_kills_the_process test spawns a real ~1s ping loop with a 300ms timeout and asserts the process is killed and timed_out=true -- this is the mechanism OpenSshExecutor::execute always routes through, not a mocked assertion.

notes: Risk score: 30/100 (medium-low). Rationale: this is the first work unit that shells out to an external process (ssh.exe) with device-supplied host/port/username, so command-injection risk is directly relevant -- mitigated by passing every argument separately via Command::args() (never a single interpolated string) and by WU005/WU006 already rejecting shell metacharacters in host/username before a Device can exist. The classify_outcome heuristic text-matches OpenSSH stderr, which is inherently a little fragile across OpenSSH versions/locales; I mitigated this by checking it against this machine's real OpenSSH client output for the two most common failure modes rather than trusting the heuristic blind, but host-key and authentication-failure message text specifically were not re-verified live (no local sshd was available to trigger them) -- worth a manual check against a real Raspberry Pi in WU008/M2 acceptance testing.

The SystemIdentity/SystemMetrics/DockerContainers command bodies are intentionally left undefined (RemoteOperation::command() returns None for them) rather than guessed at now, so the M3 work units that own metrics/Docker parsing can design the command body and parser together rather than inheriting an untested script from this work unit.
